question: Should root package metadata become the effective ClawHub license for new and historical skill versions, or should it remain separate declared-source metadata from the platform publishing license?
rationale: Current main and release history intentionally define MIT-0 as the platform license, while this PR changes both future publishing semantics and historical stored records; code review cannot determine that legal and product contract.

options.title: Separate declared and effective licenses
options.body: Store detected MIT as source-declared metadata while preserving the effective MIT-0 platform field until an explicit override and migration policy is approved.

options.title: Approve declared-license authority
options.body: Accept MIT declarations as the effective license, but require live publish/import proof, API compatibility documentation, and a dry-run plus applied backfill demonstration before merge.

options.title: Keep MIT-0-only policy
options.body: Retain the current fixed platform license and close this PR after documenting why conflicting package metadata cannot alter ClawHub's publishing terms.

recommendation.title: Separate declared and effective licenses
recommendation.body: Store detected MIT as source-declared metadata while preserving the effective MIT-0 platform field until an explicit override and migration policy is approved.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent ownership signals cover the latest-version metadata and backfill paths most affected by the decision.
